subject: ACME Bank — Region pinning & data residency clarifications

Subject: Follow-up & clarifications: Region pinning / data residency (ACME)

Hi John / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning — helpful to understand the scope. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the key open questions so we can get you precise answers from our engineering/security teams before the tech deep-dive. Attached is our short region-pinning overview (redwood_region_pinning_overview.pdf).

Questions for ACME (quick):
- Which data classes must remain in-region (US/EU/APAC) vs. which can be backed up cross-region? Please call out any legal/regulatory constraints by country.
- For cross-region failover: what trigger window is acceptable (automatic on outage or manual failover)? Any max RTO/RPO requirements?
- Backups: are encrypted cross-region backups allowed? Any restrictions on where backups may reside?
- PII & retention: retention windows by data class (e.g., transaction logs 7 yrs, customer PII 5 yrs, transcripts 1 yr).
- Logging/audit: minimum retention for audit logs and whether logs may be exported to third-party SIEMs (yes/no).
- Key management: do you require customer-managed keys (BYOK) / HSM for at-rest encryption?

Proposed next steps:
1) If you can reply with the answers above, we’ll circle back with a concrete architecture proposal and configuration options (region pinning + failover + backup plan).
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive next week (Vanessa will lead on the technical side).
3) We’ll share SOC2, network diagrams, and a draft Data Processing Addendum for legal/infosec review.

Cc’ing Marissa for procurement/contracting follow-up. Thanks —

—Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: Follow-up & clarifications: Region pinning / data residency (ACME)

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the summary — below are our initial answers. I’ve attached our PII classification and retention policy (acme_pii_requirements.pdf) for reference.

Initial answers:
- Region requirements: EU residents’ data must remain in EU for storage and primary processing. US customers’ data should remain in US. For APAC pilots we will evaluate on a case-by-case basis.
- Backups: Cross-region backups are acceptable if they are encrypted in transit and at rest. Backups must be tagged and access-controlled; backups containing EU data must remain within EU for replication copies (we can accept encrypted copies in a separate account but only if the storage is in EU zones).
- Failover: we prefer an active-passive model — automatic failover is acceptable if failover does not violate in-region storage for EU customers. RTO target is <15 minutes for core customer-facing endpoints; RPO target is <1 hour for transactional data.
- Retention: see attached; high-level: transaction records = 7 years, customer personally identifiable information = 5 years (subject to legal holds), ephemeral transcripts = 1 year unless flagged.
- Audit logs: need 3 years of retention for security/audit logs. Logs may be exported to our SIEM (Splunk) but must be delivered via secure, authenticated connections; we will provide endpoints.
- Key management: for EU production workloads we prefer BYOK (customer-managed keys) where possible. For US production we can evaluate Redwood-managed keys if mutual TLS and KMS controls are present.

We’d like a technical session (60 min) with Vanessa and your infra team to walk through the architecture and failover behavior. I can do Fri 3/28 10–11am PT or Tue 3/31 afternoon — let me know what works.

Thanks,
Priya
Senior Product Security Manager | Acme Bank
priya.singh@acmebank.com

Attachment: acme_pii_requirements.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Follow-up & clarifications: Region pinning / data residency (ACME)

Thanks Priya — good summary. Quick notes from infra/procurement perspective and suggested responses we can provide to ACME: 

Suggested approach (high-level):
- Primary region pinning per customer: Redwood supports per-customer region pinning. We can pin ACME customers to US-EAST (us-east-1) for US residents and to eu-west-1 for EU residents.
- Failover model: active-passive with geo-fenced primary region. In the event of primary-region outage we can perform an automatic failover to a pre-designated secondary region if customer approves in the DPA; otherwise we support manual failover. Automatic failover can be constrained so that EU-customer data never persists in a non-EU region — e.g., failover only within EU for EU accounts.
- Backups: encrypted snapshots can be stored cross-region, but per ACME’s requirement we will ensure backups containing EU-data are stored in EU zones only. Backups will be tagged and access-controlled.
- Retention & logs: we can set retention windows per-customer via config (transaction logs = 7y, audit logs = 3y). We can stream logs to ACME’s Splunk via secure endpoints.
- Key management: support for customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations is available for enterprise/private deployments. For hosted accounts we can also offer separated, customer-specific keys managed by Redwood with strict access controls.

Action items I’ll take:
- Draft region-pinning appendix for the DPA/MPA calling out failover modes and backup constraints.
- Pull SOC2 and network diagram pack to share with ACME before the deep-dive.
- Confirm technical leads and invite Vanessa to the session (Vanessa will handle the infra walk-through).

Aditya — please propose the meeting time and include the security/infrastructure contacts (Marco or Priya). I’ll prepare the legal/contracting notes for procurement.

—Marissa
